olivia: Quick sync — we're drafting an RFC for a serving runtime change: kernel selection policy + attention optimizations + KV cache eviction strategy. Customer Gamma asked for deterministic p99 latency for their search flow; they want launch in 6 weeks. Need to agree scope, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan. Can we get initial tradeoffs here?

alex: thanks. high level: we can do policy-based routing (latency-first vs cost-first), plus a conservative attention kernel opt. question: does Gamma need exact p99 SLA or just improvement over current?

dan: Gamma asked for p99 < 200ms across 2k token sessions. Current p99 is ~320ms for that workload on hosted small-gpu. Cost impact estimate ~+18% if we pin to low-latency kernels + disable some batching.

mira: what telemetry do we need? traces for KV hits/misses, kernel selection, batch sizes, queue time. we'll need tracing hooks before canaries.

sophia: we must add quality checks — attention kernel changes can affect token probabilities. propose a focused eval set (Gamma prompts + internal regen set). pre/post perplexity + top-1 token diffs. set quality gate: token-delta < 0.8% and no high-severity hallucination regressions on test prompts.

james: Gamma is on a Dedicated plan; they can tolerate +10% cost if p99 target met. They also need an option to opt into a pinned config in their account (so we don't affect other customers).

lisa: infra note: dedicated pools can be sized but autoscaling buffer needed for sudden load. if we reduce batching, throughput drops — so need a forecast for GPU hours. also need GPU affinity changes for kernel variants.

dan: draft rollout config (proposal):

```yaml
rollout:
  stage_1_canary: 1% traffic (Gamma only)
  stage_2_broad_canary: 10% traffic (internal + few customers)
  stage_3_gradual: 50% over 48h
  metrics:
    p99_latency_ms: '<=200'
    error_rate: '<0.2%'
    kv_miss_rate: '<=5%'
  fallback_policy: immediate-fallback-on-sla-breach -> route to standard-kernel-variant
  feature_flags:
    attention_opt: true
    kernel_selection_policy: latency_first
    kv_eviction_policy: ttl-based + size-cap(tunable)
```

dan: acceptance criteria (draft):
- p99_latency_ms <= 200 for Gamma's query distribution for 72h in staging mirror
- error_rate delta < 0.2% vs baseline
- quality gate pass (sophia's eval suite)
- no new 5xx patterns in logs; cpu/gpu saturation under 85%

mira: canary observability checklist:
- traces instrumented for kernel decisionpath
- dashboards: p50/p90/p99, evictions/sec, kv_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram
- alerts: p99 > 220ms for 15m, kv_miss_rate > 8% for 5m

olivia: good. couple of open questions for tradeoffs:
- scope: do we implement new eviction policy (ttl+size) now or keep current LRU?
- API: will customers need an explicit opt-in flag or will we auto-route based on tier?

alex: prefer opt-in for now (safer for compatibility). we can auto-route later with heuristics. eviction: TTL+size cap is easier to reason about for deterministic latency. LRU causes path variance under bursty workloads.

sophia: opt-in also helps us gather labeled traffic for eval. add a metric to capture any hallucination regressions per-customer.

james: Gamma wants opt-in plus a negotiated SLA. they also want ability to toggle to lower-cost mode quickly. add a customer toggle in Console with 2 presets: low-latency, cost-optimized.

dan: operational notes: need a config rollout flag gated in control plane + canary router rule. example control-plane flag: `runtime.latency_mode=on` per-customer.

mira: we should create a staging mirror of Gamma's traffic (replay) for a 72h run before broad canary. that'll uncover queueing artifacts.

lisa: allocate a dedicated lane in the cluster for low-latency kernels to avoid head-of-line blocking. requires scheduler change; i'll open infra ticket.

olivia: next steps:
- dan + sophia: draft PRD + RFC with acceptance criteria (due Wed EOD)
- alex + mira: list instrumentation + dashboard requirements (due Wed EOD)
- lisa: infra ticket for dedicated lane + cost forecast (due Thu)
- james: confirm Gamma's formal SLA requirements and opt-in UI ask (Thu)

olivia: quick canary gating thresholds we agreed to for RFC:
- Stage1 (Gamma mirror): p99 <=200ms for 72h, eval pass, no >0.2% error delta -> proceed
- Stage2 (10%): maintain p99 <=220ms for 24h -> proceed
- Rollback: any sustained p99 >230ms for 15m OR eval quality failure -> automatic rollback to standard-kernel

dan: adding a small checklist for the RFC to include edge-cases:
- token cache warmup behavior on long-memory sessions
- eviction race between concurrent requests
- fallback correctness when kernel variant missing on node
- telemetry gaps during gradual rollout

mira: I'll add alert runbook entries and a quick playbook for ops if rollback triggers.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging-mirror at 1733342000 for canary run :eyes:

olivia: thanks all. posting a short PRD draft in #eng-docs after this. ping me in-thread for clarifications. :thumbsup:
